title: Direct MessageReceived event
description: The normalized event delivered to exactly one local data-plane session after the receiver resolved a single endpoint. destination_endpoint is NEVER absent — resolution happened before acceptance. Broadcast events deliberately carry no endpoint routing metadata (ADR-0030), so two endpoints under one PeerId are indistinguishable as transport-level broadcast originators.

source_endpoint.description: Peer-asserted. Proves only that the authenticated PeerId claimed this route label.

destination_endpoint.description: The resolved local endpoint that accepted the message. Never absent.

media_type.description: 1..128 ASCII bytes when present. Empty is INVALID rather than an alias for absence — the content fingerprint distinguishes the two cases.

bytes.description: Application payload, unpadded base64url over IPC. `contentEncoding` is an ANNOTATION in Draft 2020-12 and constrains nothing on its own, so both the size and the syntax are asserted here. maxLength 65536 encoded characters is the 48 KiB (49,152-byte) decoded ceiling of ADR-0026. The pattern enforces the alphabet AND the legal terminal lengths: unpadded base64url can never have a length congruent to 1 modulo 4, so a value like "A" is malformed and every standard decoder rejects it — accepting it here would only defer the failure to decode time, past the point where the bound was supposed to hold. Residual: the final character's unused low bits are not constrained, which a decoder may accept or normalise; length class is what a schema can express.

received_at.description: Local receipt time in milliseconds. Excluded from the content fingerprint.
